This study establishes a method to determine a linear complement set of group codes over a finite principal ideal field within the context of cyclic codes in $F_q[x]/\langle g(x)\rangle$. The generated codes by these complements always amount to the whole space $F_q^n$. Specifically, the research presents an explicit formula for computing the dual code of a specific type of group code in terms of its generator polynomial, and it explores how this applies to cyclic codes as well.

Exact inference in a graphical model can be achieved using belief propagation, a technique applicable to various problems including finding the maximum expected payoff and optimal solutions under constraints. Despite its versatility, implementing belief propagation poses challenges due to the complexity of functions involved in graphical models. A brief function depiction framework tackles these issues by providing a concise representation for arbitrary functions. Built upon BDDs, it enables straightforward computation of marginal expectations and constrained optimization while posing a concise representation. We demonstrate its effectiveness using simple graphical models defined over binary variables.

Many everyday actions we perform rely on complex sensor systems that detect discrepancies in expected outcomes to identify misalignments or omissions. One critical application of this principle is identifying when items are lost during routine tasks such as putting away groceries. Although significant advancements have been made in tracking object progression using audio-visual cues, the specific problem of detecting missing items due to audio inflections and abrupt stops in visual progression has not received adequate attention. Our proposed system effectively addresses this challenge by synchronizing audio and visual cues in real-time and flagging potential misalignments when these signals deviate from typical coordination. Comprehensive evaluations on synthetic datasets demonstrate the robustness of our method in real-world scenarios.

Research on the shear thickening transitions of dense suspensions shows that diverse thickening behaviors converge when normalized by reference values for shear rate, shear stress, thickness, and viscosity. These transitions are governed by distinct values for the dimensionless group γ̃ = γ̄/γ̄₀. Our findings support a unified dimensionless framework that captures shear thickening in diverse suspends, even when the particle type, packing, stress response, or flow curves vary, as long as a clear thickening transition is observed.

This study develops and applies math modeling in relation to electricity consumption patterns in Pakistan, focusing on the period of load shedding from November to December 2019. Data collected through surveys was utilized to create dynamic models, incorporating static and differential equations to analyze the phase of power outages. The research also investigates the influence of user-stored devices on electricity consumption and discusses strategies for负荷shedding management.

To investigate the impact of Web search personalization on users' browsing behaviors, we conducted a controlled online study where participants were asked to perform research on specific topics after having previously customized their Google Web search results in differing ways. Unexpectedly, participants were influenced by irrelevant and blocked web pages in both their conscious choices and unconscious page selection patterns, indicating the presence of persistent subconscious effects. This indicates the significance of considering potential personalization-induced biases when evaluating a person's informed decisions.

Program synthesis, the process of automatically generating correct programs, has been extensively researched for decades. A recent study proposed using a fully convolutional neural network to identify program structures from basic flow diagrams, employing binary labels for graph elements and leveraging supervised learning. The approach, which incorporates novel layers such as an identification layer and a customized max-pooling layer, aims to create more generic program representations and has achieved improved results over previous methods, demonstrating potential for a significant milestone in program synthesis using graph element-level labels.

Diminution strategies in climate simulations are discussed here to accelerate computational efficiency by reducing model complexity through lower spatial resolution and simplified physics, thereby enabling faster climate forecasts. Employing downscaling methods enables the leverage of the strengths of general circulation models (GCMs) while simultaneously minimizing the computational overhead of regional models (RGMs). Diminution techniques encompass various techniques like nested models, simplified boundary conditions, and simplified physical parameterizations. Each downsaling approach possesses distinct advantages and limitations, which are also discussed here to help clarify the various options available for climate modeling.

This work presents detailed atomic data for specific ions, namely Os $Z-1$, Au $Z-2$, and Os $Z$ $d^8$ ($8s$) $^3H_6$ ($0 \leq Z \leq 80$), using high-precision simulations. The data obtained include energy levels, extensive rate coefficients for a range of spectral processes, and are presented in electron temperature intervals ($1 \leq T_e \leq 1000$ K) across the wavelength range ($0.2 \mu$m $\leq \lambda \leq 4 \mu$m). These results are particularly significant as they encompass parts of the electromagnetic spectrum relevant to the ejecta of kilonova events.

Radiation therapy targeting the gastrointestinal (GI) tract requires precise GI canal segmentation for effective treatment, which can be time-consuming and labor-intensive when done manually by human therapists. This study proposes an innovative and cost-efficient AI solution for automatically segmenting GI tracts in CT images of animals and humans using a U-Net deep learning model. The proposed model achieved impressive results, with validation metrics of 0.942 Dice similarity coefficient, 0.959 Average Hausdorff Distance, 98.8% Precision, 98.8% Recall, and 98.8% Accuracy. The open-source code and data are freely accessible to accelerate future research in the area.

The paper commences with basic mathematical concepts and gradually develops linear algebra framework for analyzing complex systems, like those described above, starting with simple axioms. Key ideas in understanding system information flow including flow rates, input-output connections, system responsiveness and internal system relationships are defined using fundamental mathematical frameworks. Concepts such as 'rate of flow', 'input-output relationship', and 'internal system dynamics' are precisely defined using mathematical algebra systems, leading to the development of a framework for analyzing information flow within complex systems, ultimately enabling deeper insights through detailed visualization.

A comprehensive analysis of 416 HARPS and 88 CORALIE velocity measurements, spanning from 2002 to 2021, has yielded 51 additional sub-Saturn mass planets with radii less than 1.2 times that of Earth. This discovery expands the known range of such planets beyond the gaps previously observed in the range of 1.5-2.5 times Jupiter mass and 4-8 times Jupiter mass. Despite numerous attempts, the desert previously observed in the range of 1.5-2.5 times Jupiter mass has remained elusive. We speculate that the disappearance of the desert may be attributed to an incomplete understanding of measurement inaccuracies. Additionally, we examined the radii distribution of these newly discovered planets based on their orbital periods, discovering that period-specific exoplanet sizes tend to decrease as they grow larger, suggesting that atmospheric abundances of H2-He play a significant role in determining planetary sizes for early-formed planets with较短 orbital periods.

Effective management of information access to relevant details throughout training substantially impacts supervised learning performance. In contrast to previous strategies, our proposed method, Shared Information Maximization, deliberately chooses data points that enhance understanding of relevant information. SIM's global optimization property can be directly applied within existing frameworks, like the Attention Pooling framework. However, optimizing SIM introduces a complex problem involving complex conjugate gradients. We show that data point selection can be simplified into resolving real-valued problems. Furthermore, to handle complex conjugation, we develop a memetic algorithm that combines evolutionary computation and local optimization. Evaluations on various datasets, including MNIST, CIFAR10, and ImageNet, demonstrate that Attention Regulation via Shared Information Maximization outperforms existing methods.

Stable dark matter that interacts through a scalar or pseudoscalar mediator could significantly affect stellar processes such as supernovae, neutron star mergers, and the formation of primordial black holes. This interaction would lead to a more compact state of dark matter, altering its behavior compared to the conventional understanding.

In our study, we explored how recurrent neural networks (RNNs) could be designed to mimic key properties of cerebral cortex microcircuits, focusing on the Cerebellum's Purine-Folia structure. We utilized open-source hardware, the SpiNNKk, to execute large-scale spiking neural networks, specifically 512x512 weight-connected RNNs and their 1024x1024 variants, in our Cerebellum-inspired model. The results of our research on the classic "triuph in the lottery" benchmark demonstrated that our sparse, quantized RNNs could learn significantly faster than state-of-the-art deep learning models, including Convolutional Neural Networks and standard recurrent neural networks, when evaluated on numerous cognitive tasks.

This work delves into a particular class of nilpotent algebras by examining their multiplications within a fixed vector space. To support this exploration, we also introduce some relevant definitions and findings related to affinely equivalent algebras. In addition, we employ a particular type of geometric object to characterize specific categories of algebras. Our research provides geometric descriptions for categories of 2-nilpotent algebras as well as square-zero algebras in dimensions up to four.

High-redshift Active Galactic Nuclei are believed to have developed powerful jets that produce extremely luminous electromagnetic radiation. Research indicates that cooling of these jets by intense radiation from the nuclei can actually enhance energy transfer to the particles driving the jets, which has the opposite effect on electromagnetic radiation production. This process is further complicated by the cosmic microwave background radiation, whose influence is significant at high redshifts and can lead to substantial relativistic jet output. Our analysis reveals that this effect is particularly pronounced in low-luminosity nuclei with little non-thermal radiation, suggesting an optimal range for interaction between the two systems.

A general framework is developed for classical gravity by employing a geometric approach. Separate formulations are established using the first-order Palatini method and a first-order Cartan approach, with one key formulation reducing to the well-known second-order Einstein-Cartan theory. Specifically, we describe gravity in terms of the Cartan connection 1-form and the moving coframe 1-forms, expressed through the moving frame method. We demonstrate that certain first-order and second-order Lagrangians yield the same equations when analyzed via the Cartan and the Einstein-Cartan methods, respectively. For reference, we provide form calculations in an appropriate local coordinate system and offer three distinct expressions for the second-order Einstein-Cartan Lagrangian, including two formulations involving the Cartan 2-form. By expressing the coframe as the exponential of the Cartan 1-form, we derive the third possible expression for the second-order Einstein-Cartan Lagrangian, which incorporates the Lie algebra structure constants. Lastly, a straightforward transformation enables the conversion of first-order into second-order Lagrangians.

Our new approach for registering image datasets involves combining the benefits of a discrete symmetry-based method and a modified SIFT method designed for 3D data. We register each individual image to a common coordinate system by utilizing a simplifiedSP-based method for image alignment and a register-based strategy to optimize pose parameters across multiple images. We enhance traditional SIFT descriptors with our new 3D-PISIFT method, which offers improved robustness for estimating correspondences within the multi-image context. Our framework demonstrates improved stability and superior alignment precision over existing algorithms. When compared to cutting-edge methods, our technique achieves better results on average, with a mean error improvement of 2.0 mm and significant improvements of up to 3.5 mm in specific cases. Furthermore, our approach exhibits enhanced resistance to alignment errors within a narrow range.

Our study focuses on SDSS J082239.54+304857.19, a binary system with two white dwarfs that collide periodically every 40.499 minutes. Recent data from TESS and Kepler observations revealed that this binary system undergoes eclipses and exhibits multiple oscillations, suggesting a complex structure for one of its white dwarfs. To better understand these complexities, we used light curve modeling to confirm that this binary system fits within a certain range of distances from our sun and has specific orbital characteristics. Furthermore, our analysis revealed a period of mass transfer within the system and identified possible structures for one of its white dwarfs, though we found conflicting data that require further investigation.

Traditional global evaluation methods face challenges in capturing the nuances of regional disparities in decision-making outcomes. We undertake a re-examination of standard global aggregation techniques by integrating the concept of optimal transport in a decision-making context. A new method of evaluation is proposed that utilizes the transport cost to measure the discrepancy between predicted and actual values. This discrepancy is conceptualized as a form of 'information loss' incurred during evaluation. We provide a framework for comparing different aggregation methods by establishing bounds on global and local evaluation errors. Notably, this framework reveals that commonly used techniques, such as mean, median, geometric mean, and mode, are either stochastic or non-stochastic acceptors. Specifically, this decision-maker receives satisfactory results when the actual distribution of outcomes matches the generated distribution.

We examined archival HST and Chandra data for 31 unobstructed dry active galactic nuclei located in the center of their respective host galaxies, which were sorted into different types based on their spectral characteristics. Our analysis revealed significant differences in the ellipticity of host galaxies for different AGN categories, which were more noticeably horizontal circle shaped in type S2 nuclei. However, these discrepancies in ellipticity were not corresponding to the inclination of host galaxies. Furthermore, our team also analyzed how host galaxy properties influenced X-ray emission power, which was not solely dependent on inclination but also varied based on galaxy density and morphological structure.
This paper investigates flat Rotational surfaces with the 1-type Gauss map within the 4-dimensional Euclidean space, employing it to further explore and characterize rotational surfaces.

A notable advancement in semantic segmentation via deep neural networks has been achieved through self-supervised depth estimation. Nevertheless, image-level classification benchmarks, such as Ade20K and Cityscapes, offer superior quality labels that can instruct networks more effectively than self-supervised depth estimates. We investigate whether self-supervised depth estimates can serve as a more efficient alternative to class labels for pre-training models. Our findings demonstrate that self-supervised depth estimates can serve as a high-quality label, enabling networks to reach better performance on the driving scene segmentation benchmark SceneFlow than on the cityscapes benchmark. We also explore the potential advantages of multi-task learning combinations.

Long-form numerical narrative generation is hindered by a scarcity of annotated data due to the need for domain expertise, a significant barrier to progress. This paper proposes a method that generates structured, detailed narratives within various time-based domains without relying on a predefined framework. The approach utilizes a two-stage process: a template-based model that creates a narrative's foundational structure and a transformer-based model that infers a domain-specific narrative style from unannotated data. We showcase the effectiveness of the proposed method on a time-series dataset depicting building heating control, producing narratives comparable to those of domain-expert writers across a broad spectrum of domains. The code supporting this innovation will be publicly available.

In recent years, the ATLAS experiment has made considerable advancements in the
study of particle physics, particularly in areas of new physics within B mesons.
Our objective is to present the outcomes of our most recent investigations into
the violation of CP in various B meson decays, as well as in a unique decay mode,
at the LHCb in 2012 and during the 2015-2016 period, operating under 13 TeV.
These studies include measuring differences in CP violation patterns between two
variations of the mesons, examining the rare decay of one type of B meson into its
corresponding charmless counterpart and two muons, and analyzing the decay of its
charmless counterpart into two pions and two muons.
On a Cayley tree of arbitrary degree, we examine the Ising model and demonstrate the existence of novel periodic and mildly periodic Gibbs measures.

We've developed a new class of hyperbolic Cauchy problems with coefficients that vary at a logarithmic rate and are globally solvable. This classification encompasses equations with coefficients that are lower than a certain threshold, indicating they are slightly more robust than typical parabolic equations and slightly less stable than wave equations.

Determining Word Boundaries in Japanese Continuous Text.  2.  Automatically dividing Japanese text into individual words based on established patterns using machine learning.  This approach has been successfully applied in various fields, notably including automatic translation and machine listening in the Parler Japanois system.  However, accurately dividing word boundaries in flat Japanese text remains challenging, particularly in cases where there are no numerical characters or punctuation marks to aid segmentation.  To overcome this limitation, the authors have proposed an advanced model, based on the Short-Term Memory framework, capable of retaining essential information about morphological features such as stem and inflection across a short timeframe.  By incorporating this framework with neural networks that process sequential data, the authors were able to achieve accurate and comprehensive word segmentation, including cases involving unparsed runs.  Despite incorporating multiple features, the model demonstrated minimal signs of overfitting, and its performance surpassed existing methods on carefully constructed test sets comprising both flat and segmented Japanese text.  Moreover, the results indicated that the model's efficacy in segmenting unparsed runs approached that of traditional methods designed for segmented text.

Data derived from user interactions on collaborative platforms such as Stack Overflow reveals potential opportunities for enhancing information dissemination across these digital spaces. Given the colossal scale and intricacy of Stack Overflow, identifying promising areas for improvement can be challenging. To address this issue, we introduced HaShi, a system that examines external links shared on Stack Overflow, highlighting prevalent topics and linking them to dominant discussion threads. By pinpointing external resources that are widely distributed yet potentially less effective, HaShi fosters connections between prominent Stack Overflow discussion areas and referenced resources. As a result, users can learn from these links and redistribute them towards accomplishing their stated goals. HaShi is designed to target scenarios in which users seek guidance, knowledge, or recommendations from popular websites, including professionals, educational institutions, and forums.

There has been a longstanding enigma regarding the variability of a galaxy's disk due to the observed discrepancies when attempting to recreate galaxy variability using the disk diffusion model, particularly noticeable by differences between the actual and predicted number of cluster members leaving the galaxy over time. Recent data obtained through the Multi-Unit Spectroscopic Instrument on the VLT have revealed that galaxy variability is more consistent with a model in which members leave a galaxy entirely at random, irrespective of their initial position within the galaxy. This contradicts the disk diffusion model, which anticipates variability depending on a member's initial position within the galaxy. Although some researchers have attempted to reconcile the discrepancy, their efforts have not been successful. In this study, various models have been evaluated to better understand the variability of galaxies, taking into account differences in galaxy density profiles and gravitational interactions within the galaxy system. A model in which galaxies collide during close encounters has been discovered to closely resemble the observed galaxy variability, resolving the long-standing discrepancy.

This paper examines the Climate Data Repository, a centralized platform designed to gather climate time series information from various sources. It seeks to bridge the gap between climate research and policy by standardizing climate data through a well-defined ontology and query language. To achieve this, the CD R leverages technologies such as OWL-R, RDFS, RDF, and SPARQL. Furthermore, the Climate Data Repository enables sophisticated climate analysis by incorporating rule-based reasoning. Utilizing SPARQL, users can derive meaningful insights from gathered climate data. The paper showcases the functionality of the Climate Data Repository through demonstrated queries and highlights its utility in facilitating climate change assessments, ultimately facilitating informed decisions regarding climate mitigation strategies.

Domain adaptation issues often hinder the broad applicability of biomedical NLP models. Our focus for this research is on developing an effective method for symptom event extraction from medical notes in diverse domains. We employ a "lookahead" technique, where notable elements like entities and relations are skipped during training but full note information is used for testing. This ensures the model concentrates on higher-level context connections. Our proposed method is evaluated across three datasets covering various symptom extraction tasks. Our results show it performs well on domain generalization, surpassing traditional unsupervised domain adaptation methods in both exact match and semantic understanding, demonstrating its suitability for symptom extraction across diverse domains without the need for domain-specific annotations.

Our research delves into the potential of Deep Reinforcement Learning as a viable solution for self-driving vehicles. This chapter begins by outlining fundamental Deep Reinforcement Learning concepts and班dits problems, progressing to an overview of neural networks, feature learning, and specific models, such as linear models, logistic regression, and multi-layer perceptrons. It also examines the influence of activation functions and the back-propagation algorithm for training. Furthermore, it explores the advantages of using deep reinforcement learning to tackle complex challenges and introduces key architectures, such as Q-learning and policy gradient models. Lastly, it highlights the transformative impact of these advancements on developing autonomous vehicles.

In the domain of energy-efficient computing, we utilize spiking neural networks as a solution, incorporating the unbounded dynamic range of memristive crossbar arrays in the analog domain. Our study, however, identifies a limitation in current spiking implementations: they employ spike propagation as the activation function, which lacks the ability to express negative values effectively. To overcome this constraint, we introduce a novel spiking classifier leveraging wired-in logic and exploit the variability of impedances. Our objective classifier, designed entirely in the analog domain, achieves significant reductions in energy consumption and computing time compared to its digital counterparts. Our expanded solution, compared to existing methods, showcases a 6x acceleration in inference speed, along with enhancements in convergence speed and classification accuracy.

The thermal properties of Strange Quark Stars at high temperatures, especially those containing strange, up, and down quarks, are examined through numerical analysis in this study. We investigate equilibrium quark distributions within these stars under various temperatures and strong magnetic fields, focusing on their spin-aligned states. Our research employs a Mott hasner potential to account for thermal interactions between quarks and calculates the resulting chemical potentials, pressure, and energy densities aligned with Miranshey et al's 2017 findings. We demonstrate that as the temperature rises, the UP-spin quark density decreases and reaches zero at a certain temperature threshold, whereas the DOWN-spin quark density exhibits a contrasting pattern. We also observe that both types of quark densities decrease with increased magnetic field strength. We further examine how a finite bag constant and Mott hasner potential impact these stars' mass and radius functions. We conclude by comparing our theoretical models with observational data, especially those of PSR J2215+2735, and find that our findings are consistent.

Traditional distributed computing methods designed for devices are poorly suited for individual volunteer devices due to a lack of inherent security. As a result, they are unable to offer any assurance of a device's identity, making it impossible to reward and trust them. In response, this paper presents a security framework that leverages modern browser capabilities to facilitate safe and verifiable distributed computing with individual volunteer devices. By utilizing encryption techniques and preventing various browser attacks, our method ensures the integrity of the computed framework. We further demonstrate how boundless volonteer pools can be achieved by allowing multiple users to participate through their respective browsers. In addition, techniques are outlined for bounding the volunteer computing force at a specified level. Finally, experimental results are presented, illustrating the practical security and performance of our method in actual deployments.

Relying on minimal rational interpolation, specifically the Sinc method, an advanced eigenissue solver for nonlinear problems is developed and analyzed. The proposed solver demonstrates an efficient computational cost of $\mathcal O(N \log N)$, where $N$ represents the number of Sinc points, by utilizing the fast evaluation of Sinc interpolation and estimating the eigenissues within a specified tolerance $\eta$ in $\mathcal O(\log(\eta))$ steps. Additionally, the solver exhibits convergence with a rate of $\log(\eta)/\eta$, which is shown to be independent of certain assumptions, namely the norm of the given R-matrix and its derivative, making the method particularly advantageous in situations where these variables can be quite small.

This study investigates the $\beta$-shifts that result from base $\beta$ expansions for real numbers base $\beta > 1$, particularly the ones that have a transition point in their digit sequences. The ones with transition points at the same value and rightmost digit sequence are called intermediate $\beta$-shifts, which are a subset of avaricious $\beta$-shifts, a class that has symbolic dynamical systems representing valid avaricious $\beta$-shifts. A key contribution of this study is establishing the topological transitivity of intermediate $\beta$-shifts, which were previously thought to be topologically equivalent to avaricious $\beta$-shifts, but further findings indicate this equivalence is incorrect.

Within the framework of QCD-like gauge theories, we conducted numerical investigations using lattice QCD for $SU(N_c)$ and $SO(N_c)$ theories, with $N_f$ massless fermion flavors, to examine the patterns of confinement and chiral symmetry breaking. Through an examination of the gauge field's loop factor area distribution, we were able to confirm the presence of area-law behavior in both theories, which is a definitive manifestation of confinement, within their deconfinement phases. Furthermore, through computations of the inverse of the lightest Dirac operator's eigenvalue density at zero, we were able to verify the pattern of chiral symmetry breaking in both theories, with a resulting $SP(U(N_f \times N_f))$ symmetry breaking pattern. These results, coupled with an analysis of the fermionic Polyakov loop, led to the conclusion that the lattice theories for $SU(N_c)$ and $SO(N_c)$ with massless quarks exhibit the same phenomena of confinement and chiral symmetry breaking.

To understand the predictions made by popular machine learning models such as Random Forests and Adaboost, we need to isolate the impact of individual input features on model predictions at specific data points. To achieve this, we need to consider correlations between features, which can be represented in separate attribution graphs that visualize feature importance and correlation simultaneously. However, these graphs can become complicated with large datasets, making them difficult to comprehend for humans. To address this challenge, we developed an advanced algorithm, which extracts meaningful three-node subgraphs from the attribution graph, allowing us to simplify it while preserving key characteristics such as feature importance, correlation structure, and node node relationships. We validated our approach on synthetic datasets of various difficulty levels and observed significant improvements over traditional attribution graphs, which resulted in more clear and clear model interpretations.

Machine learning, particularly when utilizing large datasets and models, is inherently vulnerable to attacks due to data and model sensitivity. Individuals or organizations capable of acquiring this information could potentially exploit it, rendering any trained model potentially compromised. Researchers have proposed utilizing Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) to mitigate this risk, although current TEE solutions are relatively expensive and not universally accessible. Our novel framework, Flatee, integrates machine learning training with TEEs to facilitate secure communication between clients and servers, relying on a single, cost-effective hardware platform known as Intel SGX, thereby minimizing costs. Flatee achieves this through an innovative federated learning approach, in which both data and models are secured within enclaves, allowing for a fully protected training process. Furthermore, our study reveals that Flatee imposes negligible additional computational overhead, specifically, only 0.1% to 20.1%, over traditional training methods.

Modern processors employ numerous optimization techniques, known as operators,
which can substantially boost system performance while using minimal extra code
space and power. As operators improve the efficiency of executing embedded code,
they also complicate the process of selecting the most effective combination for
a particular application, especially one running on small embedded systems with
limited space for code. Our novel approach automatically evaluates a wide range
of operator combinations for embedded applications, even those on such hardware
as the Arm Cortex-M4. By integrating our method, developers can access more
optimized combinations that were previously inaccessible, thus elevating the
quality of solutions achievable with these processors. Our results indicate that
incorporating operators, especially vector operators, can increase the speed of
workloads by 2 to as much as 5 times, merely by applying them to the code.

Achieving optimal performance when deploying containerized microservices can be challenging due to the intricate interactions between service calls. Current resource allocation strategies, which typically rely on straightforward metrics, often fail to account for deeper microservice behaviors, limiting their ability to deliver optimal results. Research has demonstrated that anticipating temporal patterns can significantly enhance resource allocation efficiency. However, existing neural network-based models require extensive computation to forecast future timelines, an unfeasible amount of overhead for autonomous ASR deployments. This study introduces a new deep learning approach, Timeloops, a lightweight policy model composed of circular policy layers, capable of learning and predicting temporal dependencies in ASR trajectories. Timeloops enables the exploration of past reinforcement learning experiences to forecast future rewards, thus outperforming previous models and delivering a substantial improvement in ASR performance with minimal overhead in benchmark deployments.

Tobin, Senyurek, and Krunz developed a way to separate clusters linearly in their study of formality, which uses a unique transformation to map cluster shapes into different dimensions based on their correlations. To add complexity, a new framework employs a unique transformation that maps observations onto various geometric spaces, allowing a single linear classifier to handle observations with various relationships. We investigate a k-nearest neighbor classifier within this framework and find that it achieves a minimum Bayes risk of O(1/k^(d/(d+1))) as k increases. Our work particularly reveals that observations with positive correlations can be effectively classified using a wide range of methods, and a sufficient condition for a linear classifier to be used consistently in these scenarios has been established. Additionally, for observations with negative correlations, we find that linearity may result in classification errors due to its inability to capture curvature, which our findings illustrate by comparing the risks of different classifiers.

Our previous work demonstrated that a cluster of identical stars can maintain its integrity in close proximity to a massive black hole when in the strong gravitational regime. Theoretically, this regime applies to systems with more than 5.2 $M_\odot$ black holes in our local environment. The ideal configuration, known as HE5998, involves the stars orbiting the black hole at the same radius and sharing an identical orbital plane. Simulations of this stable configuration are still sensitive to the initial conditions, and various scenarios may yield disparate outcomes. The goal of this research is to refine our understanding of stabilizing factors in such environments, particularly in relation to heap parameters. By employing numerical simulations, we aim to validate our previously proposed criteria for determining system stability. The resulting findings could potentially inform our comprehension of galactic central compact objects and their surrounding environments.

This paper presents a simple model predictive control strategy to demonstrate the value of incorporating forecasts into control algorithms on board systems. Our focus specifically lies in evaluating the benefits of leveraging forecasts in actuators with inherent limitations, such as food processors with limited capacities. Initially, a basic algorithm is developed using predictions generated by a Monte Carlo method. Subsequently, this approach is enhanced through a non-linear optimization process. Finally, a more sophisticated algorithm is created by integrating predictions from a machine learning-based estimator. All comparisons were achieved through simulations of an exemplary system, namely a processor preparing meals for astronauts on the International Space Station.

This paper delves into a prominent machine learning technique known as Independent Component Analysis, focusing on its application in sparse scenarios. We provide a comprehensive framework that enables the selection of suitable compressors for the involved nonlinear functions, encompassing both computationally efficient algorithms with precise recovery guarantees and simplified implementations that are more feasible.

A cellular automaton model is presented that incorporates colonization competition between two species, each employing distinct strategies: species A relies on local neighborhood interactions to determine its influence area, while species B's range expands until it reaches a predefined limit. Through numerical examination, it's observed that as the probability of successful invasion increases for one species, it reaches a point of exclusive dominance, whereas at lower probabilities, both species reach a dynamic equilibrium in their spatial distribution. This behavior suggests the presence of a balanced competition-colonization trade-off between the two species, where more aggressive invaders tend to occupy larger territories, whereas less aggressive ones favor a mosaic pattern of coexistence. Nevertheless, when examining temporal fluctuations in this equilibrium state, it's found that these fluctuations diminish at further removed time scales, potentially casting doubt on the long-term stability of this coexistence scenario.

We show that in abelian quantum double models, regional algebras are equivalent to von Neumann algebras associated with a specific type of inclusion with finite index. We establish that the category of regional algebras is monomorphically equivalent to mc(VN), the category of von Neumann algebras with inclusion morphisms, thereby demonstrating that the asymptotic behavior of quantum channel capacity matches that of communication capacity. Furthermore, our analysis of von Neumann algebras associated with ball-shaped regions reveals area law behavior for entanglement.

Generating fully entangled systems comprising magnons, photons, and phonons in cavity magnomechanics presents an intricate challenge. This study presents a method to achieve and sustain magnon-photon-phonon tripartite entanglement within the cavity magnomechanical system. The research investigates how linear coherent feedback circuits enhance tripartite entanglement and identifies conditions under which it arises. Notably, this study demonstrates that the presence of coherent feedback can eliminate the need for large magnon-drag coefficients typically required for entanglement generation, thus facilitating easier production of fully entangled systems. The entanglement generated in this manner can be restored when the cavity magnomechanical system interacts with the coherent feedback circuit. The tripartite entanglement measure, PPT criterion, and Gaussian entanglement criterion are employed to quantify interactions among magnons, photons, and phonons in the cavity magnomechanical system with the coherent feedback circuit.

This study presents one-loop triple-collinear splitting operators for tree-level singular matrices within $d$-dimensional QCD. These operators serve as key elements in calculating finite subtraction terms during next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N$^{3}$NLL) calculations. Derived through algebraic manipulation without leveraging known results, the presented operators expand on previous work, building upon the basis of nested sum matrices introduced by work of Catani and others.

We have addressed a long-standing query regarding the Neron Desingularization theorem's application to one-dimensional local rings, specifically whether a certain condition is met in such rings, which had been originally proven to imply finiteness in one instance. The obtained result confirms that this condition is indeed applicable to one-dimensional local rings, which was later shown to contain contentless special fibers. Consequently, this became one of the key prerequisites in Neron Desingularization, which stated that for any one-dimensional local ring, there exists a finite, non-degenerate map from an n-dimensional regular local ring to that ring, which reduces to an isomorphism in its completed field's field of fractions.
